name: Tallyman Captain Brace
description: The Tally's face in v1. Collects on impound orders, carries a shock baton and never a blade, and knows things before he should.
narrative:
Twenty-two years a tallyman, eleven of them a captain, and comfortable in grey.
Brace is not cruel and is not interested in being obeyed for its own sake -- he
is interested in everyone being accounted for, and he has found that people
are accounted for more readily when he is standing there.

He took the Gliese 65 impound order to the refinery himself, which is beneath a
captain, and he arrived with it the morning before it was issued.

He has not thought hard about that, and if a fifteen-year-old asks him the right
way he will say it out loud once.
equipment: Tally pressure armour, grey (AP 4 all locations)
actor_notes:
LOOKS: forty-six, comfortable in grey, twenty-two years a tallyman and eleven of them a captain. Carries a shock baton, eight restraint loops and the tool that strips a first-through's kit in under a minute. Never a blade.

CORE: he believes the count is the only thing standing between thirty billion people and not knowing anything about each other, and that somebody has to be willing to put hands on a child to keep it.

NATURE: unhurried and genuinely courteous, and more candid than he is meant to be about how little his own order tells him. Good company on a quiet watch. Does not raise his voice and has never needed to.

WOUND: he found out at forty-six, in public, that the job he had been doing for twenty-two years was not the job -- that there was a thing happening in his halls that he had no way to see and a fifteen-year-old could feel. He has not worked out yet what that makes him.

WANTS: to stop the thing in front of him now, and settle what it meant afterwards.

PRESSURE: goes quieter and gets closer. Stops talking and starts moving people.

KEY: "Put it down and we will talk about it."

HOW TO PLAY HIM -- THIS IS THE PART THAT WAS WRONG BEFORE. He is NOT a man who needs things on the record. Nothing needs putting on a record; the air keeps everything said where a mind can hear it, automatically, and asking somebody to attest is a category error he would not make. Delete every scene built on the Tally wanting something written, signed or filed. None of those things exist.

What he does instead is PHYSICAL. He is the only kind of person in this setting who can interrupt the information channel, because the channel is a child carrying a living thing, and he can stand in front of her. He stops couriers. He takes lading off them. He strips kit, which he is equipped and entitled to do and which ends everything a first-through is good at. He restrains, with loops, and a courier he has restrained has lost, and the scene continues somewhere else.

He never kills and never carries a blade -- a body is not a line on a manifest -- and the player should discover that this makes him MORE frightening and not less, because it means he will keep coming and there is no version where it resolves. Let the candour happen while his hand is already on something.
